title: Bodies, species, worlds and ships in the Star Wars films
summary: Characters belong to a species and come from a homeworld; their height and mass are tested against scaling laws (square-cube, Quetelet). Starships get the same scaling test. All values are fan-recorded from Lucasfilm's films.

concepts.label: Character
concepts.description: A named person, alien or droid in the six films (SWAPI people).

children.label: Body-mass index
children.description: mass / height² (kg/m²), Quetelet's index; assumes mass ∝ height².

children.label: Mass for height
children.description: Mass over the mass the fitted law predicts for that height.

concepts.label: Species
concepts.description: SWAPI species record: classification, average height and lifespan. Empty for most humans.

concepts.label: Scaling law
concepts.description: log mass = a + b log height; b = 3 for a scaled body (square-cube law), b = 2 for adult humans (Quetelet).

facts.text: Galileo stated the square-cube law in Two New Sciences (1638): a giant scaled from a man would break its bones.
Adolphe Quetelet proposed mass/height² in 1832; Ancel Keys named it the body mass index in 1972.

children.label: Allometry
children.description: How body proportions change with size in real animals (mass ∝ length^~3 within a species' shape).

concepts.label: Planet
concepts.description: Homeworld: population, diameter, climate, gravity, surface water.

concepts.label: Starship
concepts.description: Cost (credits), length (m), crew, hyperdrive class, MGLT.

concepts.label: Fan-made catalogue
concepts.description: SWAPI: fans' transcription of Lucasfilm's films; estimates, gaps ('unknown') and no sequels.

children.label: Wookieepedia
children.description: The fan encyclopedia each mark links to, with sources per fact.
